articles.title: LEDVANCE brings 116 certified devices to Home Assistant
articles.dek: Matter over Wi-Fi connects the certified lights, plugs and switches locally, with a long-term support commitment.
body: Home Assistant adds LEDVANCE to its Works with Home Assistant programme with 116 certified devices. The range spans bulbs, ceiling and wall lights, strips, outdoor lighting, plugs and wall switches, giving households a wider choice of tested devices for local control.

All of the certified devices use Matter over Wi-Fi. In the announcement, Jacqueline Ajayi says Home Assistant’s in-house team tested them over that connection and LEDVANCE has committed to long-term support. They work without a cloud service, so their ordinary control does not depend on a remote server remaining online.

The certification applies to the listed models, rather than every LEDVANCE or OSRAM product. An unlisted device may still work with Home Assistant; it has not necessarily passed the programme’s testing and requirements.

articles.title: Home Assistant enforces administrator-only access to restricted apps
articles.dek: Ordinary household accounts stop reaching app interfaces reserved for administrators.
body: Home Assistant closes a route that let a non-administrator open the interface of an administrator-only app. The app proxy checked the session cookie but did not enforce the app’s administrator restriction.

Stefan Agner makes Supervisor check the person’s role before opening a restricted app. Ordinary household accounts retain access to apps that explicitly allow them. The correction uses identity information Core already supplies, so it does not require a matching Core upgrade.

Changing an administrator’s role does not immediately revoke every running session: the cached role is refreshed when that person creates a new session or Supervisor restarts, and access also ends when the session expires.

pullRequests.title: Enforce panel_admin for ingress sessions

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps albums and playlists on their chosen recordings
articles.dek: Whole albums use one source, while an optional setting keeps originals and remasters separate.
body: Music Assistant keeps an album on one source instead of independently choosing each track from different releases or services. That avoids switching between an original, a remaster and a compilation during one album, preserving its intended gaps and loudness. If the selected source lacks a track, another copy can still fill the gap.

Service playlists, local folders and podcasts also remember the copy they were started from and try it first, even when a higher-quality copy exists elsewhere. The audio details show the originating album or playlist and link back to it. Music Assistant’s own built-in playlists and songs started on their own keep their existing source selection.

A separate advanced setting keeps remastered tracks and albums apart from their originals and from remasters made in other years. It starts off and does not separate library entries already combined. Together, the changes give collectors more control over which recording actually plays.

articles.title: Matter.js adds two-way audio to its camera dashboard
articles.dek: An optional microphone control lets viewers speak through a compatible camera.
body: Matter.js Server adds a Talk control to its camera dashboard, letting someone watching a compatible camera send audio from the browser’s microphone. Opening the live view does not ask for microphone access; talking must be switched on separately.

Ingo Fischer adds the control alongside a server interface for camera streams and snapshots. Talk requires a camera that reports two-way audio and a speaker, and a browser page served through HTTPS or localhost. A live test verified audio in both directions and that talking stopped when the microphone was switched off or unplugged.

This is support in Matter.js Server’s own dashboard and client interfaces; it does not establish camera talkback in Home Assistant. Cameras that alternate between speaking and listening have not been tested live.

articles.title: Music Assistant restores HomePod voice and touch controls
articles.dek: HomePods allowing AirPlay from the same network can pass Siri requests and taps back to the music server.
body: Music Assistant’s AirPlay tool lets a HomePod pass Siri commands and touches on its top surface back to the server when its AirPlay permission is Everyone on the same network. Those speakers could play music but their skip, pause and play requests were silently ignored.

Aiden Kwok enables the command channel for that connection mode and corrects its encryption key handling. In a standalone HomePod test running OS 27.0, a spoken skip reached the server and taps paused and resumed playback. This is Kwok’s first contribution to the AirPlay tool, reviewed by Marcel van der Veldt.

articles.title: Home Assistant reads Hase wood stoves without the cloud
articles.dek: Local readings show combustion phase, firebox temperature and when the stove needs more wood.
body: Home Assistant adds a local connection to Hase iQ wood stoves from the generation controlled by the flamemonitor app. It reads the stove directly without the vendor app or a cloud service.

The read-only connection reports combustion phase, firebox temperature, heat-up progress and combustion performance. The phase includes a needs-wood state; heat-up progress appears only during heating up, and performance only after nominal temperature is reached. Benoit Bayszczak supplies the connection in his first contribution to Home Assistant Core.

articles.title: ESPHome sets a May deadline for five older display drivers
articles.dek: Existing display configurations have until version 2027.5.0 to switch to their replacements.
body: ESPHome sets version 2027.5.0 as the removal point for five display drivers that have been deprecated since April. The build warnings name both the deadline and the replacement, giving makers a concrete date for updating their display configurations.

The ili9xxx, st7735, st7789v and qspi_dbi drivers point to mipi_spi. The rpi_dpi_rgb driver points to mipi_rgb. J. Nick Koston adds the warnings for the planned 2026.11 release, providing six months before removal.

articles.title: Home Assistant starts iCloud without waiting for old reminders
articles.dek: Completed tasks stop being fetched by default, with an option to restore them.
body: Home Assistant stops waiting for the first iCloud calendar and Reminders download during integration setup. Accounts with a large history of completed reminders could otherwise spend minutes or hours starting, or have setup cancelled altogether.

Calendar and task data load in the background, and completed reminders are excluded by default. To keep seeing those old tasks, enable Include completed reminders in the Apple iCloud integration’s options. Individual data requests also gain a five-minute timeout instead of waiting indefinitely.

articles.title: Telmore Musik joins Music Assistant
articles.dek: Subscribers gain library browsing, recommendations and playback through a new connection.
body: Music Assistant adds Telmore Musik as a music source, including sign-in, search, browsing, library synchronization, recommendations and playback. Contributors tobsorbe-droid and nicoleise tested those paths with a live account.
Mathias R builds the connection on the service’s shared backend with YouSee Musik. The existing YouSee connection is unchanged. OzGav reviewed the addition.

pullRequests.title: Add Telmore musik provider

articles.title: Music Assistant prevents playlist edits from overwriting other files
articles.dek: Local-file edits check that their destination is both inside the chosen folder and a playlist.
body: Music Assistant protects files from being overwritten through playlist editing. A playlist reference could previously point to any regular file inside a Local files source, causing an add-tracks request to append playlist text to it. With an administrator’s access and a suitably located file, the source describes a path to code execution.

Marvin Schenkel limits those operations to playlist files and verifies a provider mapping before adding it. A related correction refuses to follow symbolic links while writing a playlist, preventing the destination from escaping its configured folder. Imported playlist artwork also stops accepting local file paths.

pullRequests.title: Keep playlist edits and provider mappings to real playlists
Write playlist files only to regular files inside the library root

articles.title: ESPHome keeps disabled battery charging switched off
articles.dek: SY6970 settings stop reverting about forty seconds after startup.
body: ESPHome corrects a failure that silently re-enabled charging on devices using the SY6970 power-management chip about forty seconds after startup. The same failure could turn its status light back on after the maker disabled it.
Contributor willumpie82 keeps the chip’s watchdog refreshed independently of sensor polling, preserving those settings while the device runs. This is their first contribution to ESPHome.

Long deep-sleep periods still need explicit watchdog handling because the sleeping processor cannot refresh it. The change adds configuration and control options for that case; it does not automatically preserve the settings through every sleep configuration.

pullRequests.title: [sy6970] Service the I2C watchdog so charge/LED settings persist

articles.title: Home Assistant brings houseplant health onto dashboards
articles.dek: SmartyPlants adds soil readings, light quality and a species-based fertilizing countdown.
body: Home Assistant connects to SmartyPlants soil sensors, with each plant represented by readings for soil moisture, temperature, humidity, light and light quality. A health score and fertilizing countdown reflect the plant’s species.

The integration polls the SmartyPlants cloud service every minute. Homes reachable from the internet can optionally receive signed updates immediately as well; ordinary polling remains available without that setup. Moses Oderinde contributes the integration and its guide in his first contributions to Home Assistant Core and its website.

pullRequests.title: Add SmartyPlants integration
Create smartyplants.markdown

articles.title: Home Assistant adds Xiaomi forecasts for mainland China
articles.dek: Choose a location on a map for current conditions and daily, hourly and twice-daily forecasts.
body: Home Assistant adds Xiaomi Weather for locations in mainland China. Setup lets the owner select a location on a map and checks that weather data can be read before saving it.

The connection provides current conditions plus daily, hourly and twice-daily forecasts, refreshing every fifteen minutes. It uses an interface that Xiaomi does not officially document for external use; locations outside mainland China are not supported by this initial integration. This is Shiroki Satsuki’s first contribution to Home Assistant Core.

pullRequests.title: New integration - Xiaomi Weather

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps quick temperature adjustments from disappearing
articles.dek: Heating and humidity controls retain a pending choice when the device reports its previous setting.
body: Home Assistant stops temperature and humidity adjustments from being overwritten while a person is tapping the plus or minus buttons. A device update confirming the previous tap could replace the newer choice before it was sent, making taps appear to do nothing.

The correction covers thermostat and water-heater temperatures as well as humidifier and climate humidity controls, in cards and detail panels. It also cancels a queued change when the control switches to a different entity, preventing that setting from being sent to the wrong device.

pullRequests.title: Keep pending target temperature when entity state updates

articles.title: Music Assistant prevents crashes while using its iPhone menus
articles.dek: Removing a subtle animation avoids a reproduced fault behind about a fifth of reported TestFlight crashes.
body: Music Assistant’s mobile app disables a pop-up animation that triggered a reproduced interface crash. David Bishop reports that the fault accounted for about 20% of crashes reported through TestFlight; the menu appears directly instead of fading in.

David Bishop also addresses crashes from rapid back swipes or taps. A separate queue-menu correction targets an intermittent crash after deleting an item and opening another near the bottom of the screen. Andrii Mitnovych reviewed the changes.

pullRequests.title: Disable pop-up animation to work around Compose bug
Fix crashes when swiping back rapidly
Bound queue pop-over menu height to prevent scroll crashes

articles.title: ESPHome tracks filter life from actual use
articles.dek: A new sensor accounts for running time and operating speed, keeping its total through restarts.
body: ESPHome adds a sensor that estimates the remaining life of replaceable air or water filters from how much they are used. It accounts for both running time and variable operating speed, rather than only counting calendar days.
The remaining-life reading is a percentage from zero to one hundred, and its stored usage survives device restarts. This is a usage-based estimate, rather than a measurement of how dirty a filter is.

pullRequests.title: [filter_lifetime] Add component with sensor/lambda support for is_on …
[filter_lifetime] Add the Filter Lifetime sensor

articles.title: Home Assistant shows what last switched a Shelly device
articles.dek: A diagnostic reading distinguishes physical buttons, remote commands, timers and protection trips.
body: Home Assistant gives compatible Shelly Gen2 and newer devices a Last command source reading. It identifies whether a change came from a physical button, the Shelly app or cloud, MQTT, a timer or a protection event such as overheating.

The diagnostic sensor appears for supported components that report a source, including switches, covers and lights. It helps explain whether a device was operated locally, commanded remotely or responding to one of its own safeguards.

pullRequests.title: Add Shelly last command source sensor

articles.title: Home Assistant’s iPhone app keeps access secrets out of logs
articles.dek: Production log files hide tokens, webhook addresses and remote server URLs.
body: Home Assistant’s Apple app redacts access tokens and other sensitive connection details from logs produced by release builds. The change covers webhook identifiers, cloudhook addresses, push tokens and the widget authenticity token, alongside external and remote-interface URLs.
This reduces the private information carried by those log files. Debug builds retain their detailed logging.

pullRequests.title: Redact sensitive data from logs
